title: Auth tests for gateway-secret consumption: default-deny fixture plus explicit USE grant
answers: How do I test that a user needs USE on a gateway secret in auth tests?
how to grant gateway_secret USE permission in a pytest auth test
test invoke route with secret owned by another user
body:
Use the parametrized fixture MLFLOW_AUTH_CONFIG_PATH=fixtures/no_permission_auth.ini (default-deny) in tests/server/auth/test_auth.py.
Create the secret as its owner via POST /api/3.0/mlflow/gateway/secrets/create with basic auth, and read secret_id from resp.json()["secret"]["secret_id"].
Grant access with grant_role_permission(base, user, "gateway_secret", secret_id, "READ" or "USE") and re-post, asserting the expected status step by step: 403 before, 403 with READ only, 403 for unknown ids, then non-403 with USE.
Assert only status != 403 on the USE path, because the job backend is not wired in the test env and the handler may fail later.
Run with: uv run pytest "tests/server/auth/test_auth.py::test_issue_detection_invoke_requires_use_permission_on_secret".
applies: Basic-auth integration tests in tests/server/auth/test_auth.py that cover gateway secret permissions on routes whose handler later consumes the secret.
says: Users with read permissions should not be able to use saved gateway secrets.
Invoking an endpoint using another member's secret must require explicit use access.
Triggering a service with an unrecognized secret identifier should return a forbidden error.
Members receive permission denied when trying to run actions with someone else's credentials.
Granting use permission to a collaborator should allow them to consume the gateway credential.
search: In tests/server/auth/test_auth.py, basic-auth integration tests for routes consuming gateway secrets use a default-deny fixture and step-by-step assertions ending with an explicit USE permission grant. The test sets MLFLOW_AUTH_CONFIG_PATH=fixtures/no_permission_auth.ini, creates an owned secret via POST /api/3.0/mlflow/gateway/secrets/create to obtain secret_id, and evaluates access using grant_role_permission. Assertions check 403 before grants, 403 with READ only, 403 for unknown IDs, and only status != 403 on the USE path because unconfigured job backends may fail later; tests run via uv run pytest 'tests/server/auth/test_auth.py::test_issue_detection_invoke_requires_use_permission_on_secret'.
